name: Jet Black
shortLine: Deep, solid black. Covers all grey.
description: The deepest black. Covers all grey with a strong, even colour.
pickIf: you want all grey gone with a strong black.
skipIf: you have light skin or lots of grey. Natural Black looks softer.
suitsText: Medium and deep skin · Some or lots of grey

faq.q: Does jet black cover all grey?
faq.a: Yes. Level 1 covers grey fully.
On medium and deep skin, usually yes. On light skin or very grey hair it can look harsh, so Natural Black is softer.

faq.q: How long does jet black last?
faq.a: The colour stays, but roots show in 3–4 weeks.

faq.q: Do I need a test before dyeing?
faq.a: Yes. The NHS advises testing the dye on a strand of hair at least 48 hours before.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 1, black.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Apply on roots first, then the rest.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse well. Conditioner.

name: Natural Black
shortLine: Softer black that looks more natural. Covers all grey.
description: A soft black that looks like natural dark hair. Covers all grey.
pickIf: you want grey gone without looking dyed. The safe first choice.
suitsText: All skin tones · Some or lots of grey

faq.q: What is the difference between jet black and natural black?
faq.a: Natural black (Level 2) is a very dark brown that looks softer and more natural than jet black (Level 1).

faq.q: Does natural black cover grey fully?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Can my beard be coloured natural black too?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on "Also colour beard and moustache" in My Look.

faq.q: How often do I need a touch-up?
faq.a: Every 3–4 weeks, for the roots.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 2, very dark brown.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Apply on roots first, then the rest.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse well. Conditioner.

name: Dark Brown
shortLine: Rich dark brown. A natural, safe choice.
description: A rich dark brown, natural in daylight. Softer and warmer than black.
pickIf: you want a small, safe change that covers grey.
suitsText: All skin tones · Some or lots of grey

faq.q: Will dark brown look brown on black hair?
faq.a: It looks dark and natural indoors, with a warm brown shine in daylight.
Yes, fully.

faq.q: Is dark brown a good first colour?
faq.a: Yes. It's a small, safe change.
Roots show in about 4 weeks.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 3, dark brown.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Apply on roots first, then the rest.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse well. Conditioner.

name: Medium Brown
shortLine: Lighter brown. Shows more in sunlight.
description: A lighter brown that shows clearly in sunlight. Fresh and modern.
pickIf: you want a visible but natural change.
skipIf: your hair is very black and you want a strong change. The brown will look gentle.
suitsText: Light and medium skin · Some or lots of grey

faq.q: Will medium brown show on very black hair?
faq.a: Only lightly. For a stronger brown, very black hair may need lightening first.
Yes.

faq.q: Which skin tones suit medium brown?
faq.a: Light and medium skin.
Roots show in 3–4 weeks.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 4, medium brown.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Apply on roots first, then the rest.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse well. Conditioner.

name: Burgundy
shortLine: Dark red-purple tone. Shows most in sunlight.
description: A deep wine colour with red and purple tones. Dark indoors, red in the sun.
pickIf: you want a fun, stylish change.
skipIf: you have lots of grey or a strict office.
weekly: Wash with cool water and colour-safe shampoo.
suitsText: All skin tones · No grey or some grey

faq.q: Will burgundy show on black hair?
faq.a: It looks dark indoors and shows red-purple in sunlight.
Mostly. Grey hair can turn brighter red than the rest.
It starts to fade in 3–4 weeks. Washing with cool water helps it last.
It may be too bold for strict offices.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 4, red-violet (burgundy).
Cream on hairline and ears.
Apply on roots first, then the rest.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse with cool water. Conditioner.
barberNote: On black hair, the red shows mainly in sunlight.

name: Golden Brown Highlights
shortLine: Thin golden-brown streaks on dark hair.
description: Thin golden-brown streaks through the top. Adds shine without colouring everything.
pickIf: you want a light, fun change and have some length on top.
suitsText: Light and medium skin · No grey or some grey

faq.a: Thin streaks, lighter than your natural hair, placed through the top.
Yes. The streaks are lightened first.

faq.q: Do highlights work on short hair?
faq.a: Not really. They need some length on top to show.
They grow out over 6–8 weeks.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Pick thin strands on top with a comb.
Lighten strands to Level 6–7.
Use foil or highlight cap.
Check every 10 min. Stop at golden brown.
Rinse. Toner if too orange. Conditioner.

name: Ash Grey / Silver
shortLine: Light grey or silver all over. Bold look.
description: Light grey or silver all over. A bold fashion look that needs bleaching first.
pickIf: you want the boldest colour change and have time for it.
skipIf: your hair is damaged or your scalp is sensitive.
weekly: Purple shampoo 1–2 times to keep it silver.
nextVisit: in 2–3 weeks for toner, 3–4 weeks for roots
suitsText: All skin tones · Any amount of grey

faq.q: Why does silver hair need bleach?
faq.a: Dark hair has to be lightened almost to white before the silver toner can show.
Over time it can. Purple shampoo keeps it silver.
It can make hair dry and weak. Deep conditioner helps, and damaged hair should not be bleached.

faq.q: How long does it take at the shop?
faq.a: 2–3 hours, sometimes over 2 visits.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Check scalp: no cuts or wounds.
Bleach whole head to Level 9–10.
Check every 10 min. Stop if burning.
Rinse. Then ash or silver toner.
Rinse. Deep conditioner.
barberNote: Best done by a colour expert. May need 2 visits. Tell the customer to use purple shampoo.

name: Grey Blending
shortLine: Softens grey without hiding it fully. Looks natural.
description: Softens grey without hiding it fully, for a natural salt-and-pepper look.
pickIf: you want to look fresher, not dyed, with no hard root line.
suitsText: All skin tones · Some or lots of grey

faq.a: A short, gentle colour that softens grey without hiding it fully.

faq.q: Will people notice I coloured my hair?
faq.a: Usually not. It looks like you naturally have less grey.

faq.q: Will there be a hard root line?
faq.a: No. It fades slowly over 4–6 weeks.
15–20 minutes.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 3–4, semi-permanent.
Apply on grey areas.
Short time: 5–10 min only.
Goal: less grey, not zero grey.
Rinse well.

name: Blue-Black
shortLine: Black with a cool blue shine in the light.
description: A deep black with a cool blue shine in sunlight. Covers all grey.
pickIf: you want a glossy black with a stylish twist.
suitsText: Medium and deep skin · Any amount of grey

faq.a: Indoors it looks black. In sunlight it shows a cool blue shine.
Yes, fully.
It can look harsh. Natural Black is softer.
Roots show in 3–4 weeks.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Colour: Level 1, blue-black.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Apply on roots first, then the rest.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse well. Conditioner.

name: Ash Brown
shortLine: Cool brown with no red or orange. Soft and modern.
description: A cool, soft brown with no red or orange. Often seen with Korean-style cuts.
pickIf: you want a modern brown that still looks natural.
weekly: Purple or ash shampoo once, to keep it cool.
suitsText: Light and medium skin · No grey or some grey

faq.a: A cool brown with no red or orange in it.

faq.q: Why can ash brown turn orange?
faq.a: Dark hair has warm tones underneath that show as the colour fades. Ash or purple shampoo helps.

faq.q: Do I need bleach for ash brown?
faq.a: Very black hair may need light bleaching first.
Mostly. It works best with little or no grey.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Very black hair: light bleach first, to Level 5–6.
Colour: Level 5, ash.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse well. Conditioner.

name: Copper
description: A bright, warm orange-brown that stands out in any light.
skipIf: you have lots of grey or a strict office.
weekly: Wash with cool water and colour-safe shampoo.
suitsText: Light and medium skin · No grey or some grey

faq.q: Will copper show on black hair?
faq.a: Only after light bleaching. Without it, the colour barely shows.
It fades in 3–4 weeks. Washing with cool water helps.
Yes. It needs regular top-ups to stay bright.
Mostly. Grey hair turns bright copper.

barberSteps: Ask: itching from dye before? If yes, stop.
Cream on hairline and ears.
Light bleach to Level 6–7.
Rinse. Then colour: copper.
Wait time: as on the box.
Rinse with cool water. Conditioner.

name: Henna (Mehndi)
shortLine: Natural plant colour. Turns grey hair red-orange.
description: A natural plant colour. Turns grey hair red-orange and gives dark hair a red shine.
pickIf: you want a natural colour with no chemicals.
skipIf: you may want a chemical colour later. It is hard to change after henna.
suitsText: All skin tones · Some or lots of grey

faq.q: Is henna better than hair dye?
faq.a: Pure henna is plant-based, but on grey it only gives red-orange, and it's hard to change later.
No. Its paste contains high levels of PPD, which can cause skin reactions, according to the NHS. Use pure henna only.

faq.q: How long does henna stay on?
faq.a: 1–2 hours.

faq.q: Can I dye my hair after henna?
faq.a: The result can be patchy or an unexpected colour. Tell your barber you've used henna.

barberSteps: Use pure henna only. Never "black henna".
Ask: itching from henna before? If yes, stop.
Apply paste on roots first, then the rest.
Cover hair with a cap.
Wait 1–2 hours.
Rinse with water only. No shampoo for 1 day.
